title: Ten Shapes, and Two That Lie
label: ch:bn-digits
canDo: I can read any number written in Bengali digits off a page -- a price, a year, a house number -- and I know exactly which two of the ten shapes my own reading will get wrong.

payoff.summary: Complete BN-R28-read-a-number: read a price off a shirt tag, read a year, and read a page number made of all four difficult shapes without hesitating.
payoff.note: The digits have no citable stroke order -- HL-C212 found Commons carries animations for every Bengali VOWEL and none for any consonant, and the same search finds nothing at all for the digits -- so every lesson here teaches the SHAPE against something the reader already holds, cites the Unicode Bengali chart, and CLAIMS NO PEN PATH, exactly as BN-W05-tha and BN-W06-nya do. The order is by what the reader can bring: the two shapes that agree with the Western digit of the same value (zero, two), then the one that collides with a TAUGHT LETTER (three against o), then the three that carry nothing (one, five, six), then the two false-friend PAIRS, each trap taught immediately after the Bengali digit whose value its shape suggests -- eight then four, nine then seven. The rule lesson ships both edges: eight shapes may be trusted, two may not.
